items.summaryZh: 托托·沃尔夫自2013年以来一直是梅赛德斯F1的领军人物，但现在他正在为退出车队做准备。

items.originalTitle: Toto Wolff reveals he is actively vetting “two or three people” to replace him at Mercedes
detailZh: 托托·沃尔夫透露他正在积极物色“两到三人”来接替他在梅赛德斯的工作
沃尔夫承认他的巨大运营角色可能将被两名或三名当前团队成员分担
对于梅赛德斯车迷来说，这里是关于银箭的最新消息，包括来自Brackley和Brixworth的F1新闻、车手更新、赛车发展和比赛分析
自2013年以来，托托·沃尔夫一直是梅赛德斯F1的领军人物，政治肌肉和战略支柱，引导Brackley车队通过了一个前所未有的统治时代。然而，随着这项运动的扩展和艰苦的24站赛程对身体造成的压力，这位亿万富翁车队老板正在积极为最终退出维修区做准备
在Cheeky Pint播客的最新一期节目中，沃尔夫详细介绍了他的继任计划。与一些体育高管为了保护自己的传奇而紧紧抓住权力不同，沃尔夫坚称他严格专注于长期稳定。
“对我来说，你知道，留下遗产……对我来说，重要的是做对家庭和车队最好的事情，这意味着要考虑未来的结构，这样这个车队在没有我的情况下也能生存，”他解释道。
因为沃尔夫既是车队负责人又是赛车运动部门的CEO，直接接替他的人实际上是不可能的。工作负荷包括技术监督、激烈的商业谈判和车手管理。
“我相信我的工作将分给两三个人，我现在正在对他们进行审查，我认为他们在各自的领域都做得很好，”沃尔夫确认。
F1赛车场在2023年底实际上已经短暂预览了这种分权领导结构。当沃尔夫因膝盖手术缺席日本和卡塔尔大奖赛时，他暂时将赛道现场运营职责交给了通讯总监布拉德利·劳德和前车手发展主管杰罗姆·达姆布罗西奥。随着达姆布罗西奥最近加盟法拉利，内部争夺沃尔夫未来领导结构一席之地的竞争非常激烈。
沃尔夫与INEOS和梅赛德斯-奔驰共同拥有梅赛德斯F1车队33%的股份，所以他不会在放弃车队负责人头衔后从赛车场消失。
“如果我继续拥有它，干净的分手可能是不可能的……所以这种执行或非执行主席职位可能发生，但必须非常精确地发生，因为你不能置身事外并干涉日常业务，”他指出。
在职业体育中，前老板常常通过在车库上空盘旋和质疑战略决策来破坏他们的继任者。沃尔夫坚决表示，他不会成为一个有毒的板凳经理。
“你需要确切地知道你的角色，这并不意味着从外面射击，成为坐在看台上说别人做错事的人...你不能直接联系车手...这并不是关于干涉日常事务，这就是我未来想要达到的目标，”沃尔夫承诺。
detailEn: Toto Wolff reveals he is actively vetting “two or three people” to replace him at Mercedes
Wolff admits his massive operational role will likely be split among two or three current team members
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

Toto Wolff has been the face, the political muscle, and the strategic anchor of Mercedes F1 since 2013, guiding the Brackley squad through an unprecedented era of dominance. However, as the sport expands and the physical toll of a grueling 24-race calendar sets in, the billionaire team boss is actively laying the groundwork for his eventual exit from the pit wall.

In a recent appearance on the Cheeky Pint podcast, Wolff detailed his succession plan. Unlike some sports executives who cling to power to protect their own legend, Wolff insists he is strictly focused on long-term stability.

"For me, it is not important, you know, to leave a legacy... for me it's important to do what's best for the family and to do what's best for the team, and that means looking at the structure going forward where this team can live without me," he explained.

Because Wolff acts as both the Team Principal and CEO of the motorsport division, directly replacing him is practically impossible for a single individual. The workload spans technical oversight, intense commercial negotiations, and driver management.

"I believe that my job is going to be divided between two or three people that I'm vetting at the moment that I believe are already doing a great job with all of their strengths in various areas," Wolff confirmed.

The Formula 1 paddock actually saw a brief preview of this divided leadership structure in late 2023. When Wolff missed the Japanese and Qatari Grands Prix due to knee surgery, he temporarily handed operational trackside duties to Communications Director Bradley Lord and former driver development head Jerome d'Ambrosio. With d'Ambrosio recently departing for Ferrari, the internal race to secure a piece of Wolff's future leadership structure is highly competitive.
Because Wolff owns a massive 33% stake in the Mercedes F1 team alongside INEOS and Mercedes-Benz, he isn't simply going to vanish from the paddock when he relinquishes his Team Principal title.

"A clean break is probably not possible if I continue to own it... so that kind of executive or non-executive chairmanship is something that may happen, but it needs to happen in a very, very precise way because you can't be on the sidelines and interfere into the daily business," he noted.

It is incredibly common in professional sports for former bosses to undermine their successors by hovering over the garage and second-guessing strategic calls. Wolff is adamant that he will not become a toxic armchair manager.

"You need to exactly know your role, and that doesn't mean shooting from the outside and being the one that sits on the grandstand and says you've screwed up... you can't call the drivers directly... It's not about interfering into the daily business, and that's how I would aim to be in the future," Wolff promised.

items.originalTitle: Inside COTA's Turn 1 clubhouse and its plans to build a second track
detailZh: COTA的1号弯道俱乐部及其建设第二条赛道的计划
2026年，作为一级方程式美国大奖赛的举办地，美国赛车场的外观将有所不同，因为赛道逐渐完成其转变为全年娱乐场所的过渡。一个主题公园、一个新的会员俱乐部以及未来的驾驶课程是最新增的项目
对于观看F1美国大奖赛报道的观众和电视观众来说，这很难错过。今年，美洲赛车场的1号弯道看起来与以往大不相同，因为新增了一个巨大的多层俱乐部。通过一条横跨赛道的缆车与主维修区相连，这个周末，这座新的接待设施成为了F1奢华的Paddock Club的延伸。从1月2日起，它将成为一个全年仅限会员的俱乐部，被称为'The Circuit'，因为场地将在明年开始转为私人场所
'这并不是传统意义上的年度会员资格，'COTA赛车运动高级副总裁Parris Mullins说。它更像是一个乡村俱乐部。有年度会费来维护设施和支付人员工资，但入会费是一次性支付，实际上提供的是终身会员资格
“在过去24小时内，我们收到了50多份额外的投稿，而这还是在比赛周末之前。在比赛周末之前，大约有600人联系我们。我们与大约140人进行了一对一的交谈，许多人已经开始支付定金并签署合同。”
“永远不会超过300名成员。我们将北美会员限制在250名。剩余的50个名额将是国际和公司会员的混合。”
“从COTA新1号弯道俱乐部的视角。”
“这个新设施不仅仅是COTA主席Bobby Epstein的创意。它符合F1管理层的全面推动，让赛事显著增加他们的接待服务。‘我们的合同续签也很大程度上依赖于这一点，’Mullins补充道。‘我们需要改善会员的体验和Paddock Club客人的体验。F1对此做出了重大承诺。这项运动已经发展壮大，某些市场需要这类设施。他们必须不断提高他们提供的服务。’”
COTA决定私有化带来了一些副作用，现在该场地不再对赛道日或地区驾驶俱乐部开放。但前景中有一个解决方案。在现有F1赛道北部的空地上，COTA已经制定了先进的计划，建造一个第二赛道，这个赛道较短，适合汽车和摩托车使用。
"将建造第二条赛道，主要是因为我们认识到，我们正在取代自赛道开放以来一直与我们合作的许多人和组织，" 毛林斯解释道。"对我们来说，在本地地区发展赛车运动非常重要。我们不会建造另一个FIA一级设施，因为没有这个需求。相反，我们希望建造一些适合本地赛车运动社区的东西，让他们能够继续使用赛道，并以更低的价格点获得使用机会。
"COTA显然具有声望。我知道人们喜欢能够说他们在大奖赛赛道上开过车，我们对此表示遗憾，除非他们是会员，否则这种情况将不再可能。但我们希望给人们一个可以驾驶、享受赛车运动并继续在基层参与的地方。
虽然细节仍然很少，但赛道的未公开布局已经被定义。COTA也对新建的赛道持开放态度，该赛道按照FIA三级标准建造，适合赛车、跑车和入门级单座赛车，可以举办较小的赛车运动系列赛。但毛林斯认为，由于不需要迎合F1赛车，因此有机会设计一个更适合高性能跑车及其驾驶者的赛道。
“我们希望创造一些与大奖赛赛道不同个性的有趣事物。COTA 是围绕一个主要的赛事周末的需求而建造的。我希望它有一些我们这里没有的弯道。例如，我们没有弯道，所以我认为新的赛道应该有一个。它还应该有一个标志性的S形弯道。我们希望有人们可以在他们带来的车上享受的特点。布局应该更适合他们。”
当被问及次要赛道的时间表时，穆林斯不想承诺一个确切的日期，但有一种紧迫感，不希望让当地驾驶和汽车俱乐部在没有赛道的情况下等待太久。
“我们仍然需要最终确定一切，并与城市一起完成这个过程，”他说。“我们已经足够接近，可以放心地说我们希望尽快完成。我们不希望当地赛车运动社区在没有设施的情况下等待太久，但我们也需要确保项目正确。”"
COTA 仍然将自己视为“人民的比赛”，在 F1 周末有高达 44 万人的观众人数，通过逐渐将整个场地变成一个巨大的主题公园，组织者希望利用 Netflix 时代后 F1 的变化人口。其中一些可以非常直接地实现，新的 COTALAND 游乐设施与赛道的第三部分并行运行。但大奖赛也继续其传统的大型晚间音乐会，吸引奥斯汀流行的大学体育和美食文化。”
获得到2034年的新F1合同为COTA提供了长期稳定的保障，使其能够将投资转化为一年四季都能为赛道带来收入的方式，同时举办F1、MotoGP、WEC以及从2027年开始的Formula E。COTALAND符合这一规划，专属会员俱乐部和副赛道也是如此。
但COTA并没有忘记，其核心业务是在周末期间让成群的F1粉丝得到娱乐。Mullins承认说：“F1提供赛道上的动作。我们的任务是补充这些动作之间的空档。”音乐会就是第一步。Bobby用这些音乐会做的事情真的是开创性的。
“最终，这是体育，但也是娱乐。我们想要娱乐人们。”
detailEn: Inside COTA's Turn 1 clubhouse and its plans to build a second track

Formula 1's United States Grand Prix venue has a different look in 2026 as the circuit gradually completes its transition into a year-round entertainment venue. An amusement park, a new members club and future driving course are the latest additions

For spectators and TV viewers tuning into coverage of F1's US Grand Prix, it's been hard to miss. Turn 1 of the Circuit of the Americas has a distinctly different look to it this year with the addition of a mammoth multi-storey clubhouse. Connected to the main paddock area via a cable car that crosses the track, this weekend the new hospitality structure serves as an extension of F1's swanky Paddock Club. From January 2 it becomes a year-round members-only club, dubbed 'The Circuit', as the venue turns private at the start of next year.

"It isn’t an annual membership in the traditional sense," says Parris Mullins, COTA’s Senior Vice President of Motorsports. It’s much more like a country club. There are annual dues to maintain the facilities and cover staffing, but the initiation fee is a one-time payment that essentially provides a lifetime membership.

"We’ve had more than 50 additional submissions in the past 24 hours, and that was before this race weekend. Before this race weekend, around 600 people had reached out. We’ve had one-to-one conversations with approximately 140 of them, and many have started putting down deposits and signing contracts.
"There will never be more than 300 members. We’re limiting North American membership to 250. The remaining 50 places will be a mix of international and corporate memberships."
A view from COTA's new Turn 1 clubhouse.

The new facility isn't just COTA president Bobby Epstein's brainchild alone, though. It fits a calendar-wide push by F1 management for races to significantly ramp up their hospitality offerings. "A lot of our contract renewal was dependent on this as well," Mullins adds. "We needed to improve both the members’ experience and the experience for the Paddock Club guests. F1 has made a big commitment to it. The sport has grown, and certain markets demand these kinds of amenities. They have to keep improving what they offer."

COTA's decision to go private has some side effects, with the venue now no longer available for track days or for regional driving clubs. But there's a solution on the horizon. On an empty plot of land to the north of the existing F1 track, COTA has crafted advanced plans to build a second, shorter circuit designed for both cars and motorcycles.

"A second track will be built, primarily because we recognise that we’re displacing a number of people and organisations that have been partners of ours since the circuit opened," Mullins explains. "Growing motorsport, particularly in the local area, is very important to us. We’re not going to build another FIA Grade 1 facility because there’s no need for one. Instead, we want to build something that suits the local motorsport community, allows them to continue using a circuit and gives them access at a much lower price point.

"There’s obviously prestige associated with COTA. I know people love being able to say they’ve driven their car on the Grand Prix circuit, and we’re sorry that this won’t always be possible unless they’re members. But we want to give people somewhere they can drive, enjoy motorsport and continue participating at a grassroots level."

While details remain sparse, the circuit's undisclosed layout has already been defined. COTA is also open to the new circuit, built to FIA Grade 3 standards suitable for touring cars, sportscars and entry-level single-seaters, hosting smaller motorsports series. But by not having to cater to F1 cars, Mullins feels there is an opportunity to come up with a track more suited to high-performance sports cars and the people who drive them.

"We want to create something fun with a different personality from the Grand Prix circuit. COTA was built around the requirements of a single major race weekend. I’d like it to have corners we don’t have here. We don’t have a banked corner, for example, so I think the new circuit should have one. It should also have an iconic chicane. We want features that people can enjoy in the kinds of cars they bring to the track. The layout should suit them much better."

When asked about the timelines for the secondary track, Mullins didn't want to commit to a firm date, but there is a sense of urgency not to leave local driving and car clubs without a track for too long.

"We still need to finalise everything and work through the process with the city," he says. "We’re far enough along that we’re comfortable saying we want to get it done sooner rather than later. We don’t want the local motorsport community to go without a facility for too long, but we also need to get the project right."

COTA still sees itself as the "people's race" with its enormous spectator numbers of up to 440,000 across the F1 weekend, and by gradually turning the entire venue into one giant theme park the organisers want to lean into F1's changed demographic in the post-Netflix era. Some of that can be taken quite literally, with the rollercoaster rides of the new COTALAND amusement running alongside the circuit's third sector. But the grand prix also continues its tradition of big-name end-of-day concerts, roping in Austin's popular college sports and food culture.

Earning a new F1 deal to 2034 gives COTA the long-term stability to write off those investments, and turn them into ways to make the circuit a year-round source of revenue alongside hosting the likes of F1, MotoGP, WEC and - from 2027 - Formula E. COTALAND fits into that picture, and so does the exclusive members club and the secondary track.

But COTA hasn't forgotten that its core business is to keep the hordes of F1 fans entertained over a weekend. "Formula 1 provides the on-track action. Our job is to complement that between sessions," Mullins acknowledges. The concerts were the first step. What Bobby did with those was really groundbreaking.
"At the end of the day, this is sport, but it’s also entertainment. We want to entertain people."

media.altZh: 维斯塔潘对Q3抓地力下降感到困惑，但奥斯汀展现红牛进步 · 第 1 张

items.originalTitle: Max Verstappen puzzled by Q3 grip loss, but Austin shows how far Red Bull has progressed
detailZh: 维斯塔潘对Q3抓地力下降感到困惑，但奥斯汀展示了红牛的进步
维斯塔潘可以解释为什么他的第二次Q3跑得困难，但不知道为什么第一次跑失去了那么多抓地力。尽管两位车手都不完全满意，红牛仍然获得了第二和第三名——这是车队复苏的迹象
在奥斯汀，争夺杆位的位置一度看起来将在维斯塔潘和法拉利之间展开。然而，到了排位赛结束时，斯库德里亚未能将任何一辆车送入前三名，而基米·安东内利出人意料地成为了一名竞争者
维斯塔潘只能接受第二名，他在车队的媒体休息室中的总结很清楚：是的，红牛车手当然可以接受这个起跑位置，但仍有更多的潜力可以挖掘
那在Q2的圈速中表现得尤为明显，维特斯坦普斯给他的对手留下了深刻印象。在用了一组磨损的轮胎后，这位荷兰人在新轮胎的对手中速度更快，使得连续第三次获得杆位似乎触手可及。
当Motorsport.com问维特斯坦普斯为什么Q3的画面与第二阶段的预赛如此不同时，这位四次世界冠军解释道：
“我只是不再有同样的抓地力了。就是这样简单。我无法再像之前那样在慢弯中保持我想要的速度。这显然是我们需要理解的事情，因为其中肯定还有更多。我只是无法在Q3中从车上找到它。”
风向似乎在那个故事中起到了重要的因素。在Q3的最后几分钟，许多车手被风力影响，这解释了为什么只有三次在第二次跑道上有所改进。兰多·诺里斯谈到了他驾驶生涯中遇到的最强烈的侧风，这导致他在提前作为预防措施刹车后仍然锁定了轮胎。
维斯塔潘澄清说，然而，这并不能解释Q3的全部故事。
在最后一段比赛中，风真的很大，但第一段比赛并不是这样。所以我真的不明白为什么这么令人失望。但无论如何，如果这还足以获得第二名，那就没问题了。
法拉利的速度在Q3中也下降了，查尔斯·勒克莱尔——顺便提一下，就像乔治·拉塞尔一样——指出，增加的云层和下降的赛道温度使得倍耐力轮胎略偏离了它们理想的运行窗口。
红牛车队在具有挑战性的日子里也不再落后了。
在奥斯汀的排位赛中，尽管两位车手对赛车的感觉并不满意，但车队仍然设法在发车线上获得了第二和第三的位置。
这与本赛季上半赛季形成了鲜明的对比，那时红牛在困难的日子里往往会滑落到第七和第八位——正好在由四支领先车队组成的集团后面。
维斯塔潘也承认了这一点，并认为在奥斯汀的排位赛从某种程度上代表了车队最近的重振旗鼓。
“是的，绝对是这样。在过去几个周末，赛车有了很大的改进，这是显而易见的。正如我在过去几个周末所说的那样，一些赛道会更适合我们一些。我认为这个赛道还不错，但我认为新加坡和马来西亚显然更适合我们的赛车。”
尽管在奥斯汀的比赛中，维特斯滕的赛车速度在周五看起来相当令人尊敬，这让他对周日充满信心。
"通常是的。在比赛中判断谁真正最快有点困难，但过去几个周末我们的表现相当不错。我希望我们车上的设置是正确的方向。"
起跑仍然是红牛的一大疑问，尽管在起跑线内侧的第二位提供了机会，如果维特斯滕能够顺利起步。
"是的，但我不会过多考虑这一点。如果第一个弯道发生超车，那就发生了。如果没有，那么比赛还很长，很多事情都可能出错或正确。如果你有良好的平衡和足够的车速，你可以通过策略或甚至通过在赛道上超车来比赛。"
detailEn: Max Verstappen puzzled by Q3 grip loss, but Austin shows how far Red Bull has progressed

Verstappen can explain why his second Q3 run was difficult, but does not know why he lost so much grip on the first run. Red Bull still secured second and third despite neither driver being entirely happy – a sign of the team's resurgence

In Austin, the battle for pole position looked for a long time as though it would be between Max Verstappen and Ferrari. By the end of qualifying, however, the Scuderia had failed to get either car into the top three, while Kimi Antonelli emerged as a surprise contender.

Verstappen had to settle for second place, making his conclusion during the Dutch media session in the paddock clear: yes, the Red Bull driver could certainly live with that starting position, but there was still more potential to be unlocked.

That was especially evident from the Q2 lap with which Verstappen impressed his rivals. On a set of scrubbed tyres, the Dutchman was faster than some drivers from the other top teams on fresh rubber, making a third consecutive pole position seem within reach.
When Motorsport.com asked Verstappen why the picture in Q3 was so different from the second qualifying segment, the four-time world champion explained:

"I just didn't have the same grip anymore. It's as simple as that. I simply couldn't carry the speed that I wanted through the slow corners anymore. That's something we obviously need to understand, because there was for sure more in it. I just couldn't get it out of the car in Q3."

The wind appears to have been an important factor in that story. In the closing minutes of Q3, many drivers were caught out by gusts of wind, explaining why there were only three improvements on the second runs. Lando Norris spoke of the worst gusts of wind he had ever experienced behind the wheel, which caused him to lock up despite braking earlier as a precaution.
Verstappen clarified, however, that this could not explain the whole story of Q3.

"On the final run, the wind was really bad, but not on the first run. So I don't really understand why it was so disappointing. But anyway, if that's still good enough for second place, then that's okay."

Ferrari's pace also dropped away in Q3, with Charles Leclerc – like George Russell, incidentally – pointing to the increased cloud cover and falling track temperature, which pushed the Pirelli tyres slightly outside the ideal operating window for them.
Red Bull no longer falls away on challenging days

Qualifying in Austin was nevertheless revealing about the progress Red Bull has made in recent weeks, particularly since the Baku upgrade. On a day when neither driver was particularly happy with the feeling in the car, the team still managed to secure second and third places on the grid.

That marks a considerable contrast with the first half of this season, when Red Bull would often slip towards seventh and eighth on a difficult day – right at the back of the group comprising the four leading teams.
Verstappen acknowledged this too and recognised that qualifying in Austin was, in that sense, representative of the team's recent resurgence.

"Yes, absolutely. The car has been a lot better over the last few weekends, that's clear. And as I've said over the past few weekends as well, some circuits will simply suit us a little better than others. I think this one is still okay, but I think Singapore and Malaysia were clearly better for our car."
Nevertheless, Verstappen's race pace in Austin looked more than respectable on Friday, giving him confidence heading into Sunday.

"Normally, yes. It's a bit difficult to judge who's really the fastest in race pace, but over the last few weekends it's been pretty good for us. I hope the set-up we have on the car is the right direction for the race."
The start remains a major question mark for Red Bull, although second place on the inside of the grid offers opportunities if Verstappen manages to get away well.

"Yes, but I don't think about that too much. If an overtake happens in the first corner, then it happens. And if it doesn't, then it's still such a long race in which so many things can go right or wrong. If you have a good balance and enough speed in the car, you can race here through strategy or even by overtaking someone on track."
